newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CSR says to keep timber products business.
newsitem.headline: CSR says to keep timber products business.

text.p: CSR Ltd said on Monday it planned to keep its timber products business which previously had been put up for sale through an international tender.
CSR said shareholder value would increase by A$350 million over the next two years through an improvement programme planned for the division.

CSR said the programme includes exploring a range of opportunities within the industry to improve its competitiveness. "We believe this is the best way of delivering shareholder value," managing director Geoffery Kells said.
"Shareholder value of more than A$350 million will result from implementation of the improvement programme over the next two years," Kells said in a statement.
He said over the next five years, Australia would be moving from being a net importer of timber to a net exporter, as significant plantation resource matured.
"This is a significant structural change in the Australian timber industry," Kells said.

"Prices and volumes for softwood timber and wood panel products are now at a low point in the business cycle. We expect these to recover as the housing industry gains strength and as new capacity in world medium density fibreboard markets is absorbed," he said.

CSR Timber is Australia's largest manufacturer and marketer of timber products and the country's only fully integrated timber producer. At 3.20 p.m. (0520 GMT), CSR shares were three cents lower at A$4.77. -- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
